ntc.title: NTC thermistor
ntc.description: Temperature from a resistance that changes with heat, in a voltage divider with 10 kΩ. Responds quickly and can be immersed.
ntc.orientation: Position of the thermistor in the divider
ntc.ntc5v: NTC between 5 V and the pin (as in the Elegoo kit)
ntc.ntcgnd: NTC between the pin and GND
ntc.tAmb: Ambient temperature Tₐ, for ln(T − Tₐ)
ntc.wiring: Voltage divider with a 10 kΩ resistor; the midpoint goes to {pin}.

dht.description: Temperature, relative humidity and dew point. At most 1 reading per second (DHT22: every 2 s).
dht.wiring: DATA to {pin}, VCC to 5 V, GND to GND. The 3-pin module already has the pull-up; the bare 4-pin sensor needs 10 kΩ between DATA and 5 V.

sonar.title: HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor
sonar.description: Distance from the time of flight of an ultrasonic pulse, from 2 cm to 4 m; velocity and acceleration are derived from it.
sonar.tAir: Air temperature, for the speed of sound
sonar.window: Smoothing of v and a (points per side)
sonar.origin: Origin of positions (distance from the sensor)
sonar.wiring: Use a large, flat target. Several ultrasonic sensors interfere with each other: point them in different directions.

gps.description: Position, altitude and speed from a 9600-baud serial GPS module (e.g. Velleman VMA430). Works only outdoors, with a clear view of the sky.
gps.pinTxNote: optional connection; the pin stays reserved anyway
gps.minSats: Minimum satellites to accept a position
gps.maxHdop: Maximum accepted HDOP (lower is more accurate)
gps.wiring: Antenna with the ceramic side facing the sky. The first fix outdoors takes from 30 s to a few minutes; once it has one, the module's LED blinks.

analog.title: Analog voltage
analog.measures: voltage (0–5 V) or a calibrated quantity
analog.description: Any signal between 0 and 5 V (potentiometer, pressure or force sensor); with a linear calibration it becomes a physical quantity.
analog.wiring: Signal to {pin}, GND shared with Arduino. Only between 0 and 5 V: never higher voltages, never mains power.

ldr.title: Photoresistor (light)
ldr.description: Relative brightness (0–100 %) from a photoresistor in a voltage divider: it does not measure lux.
ldr.ldr5v: Between 5 V and the pin (more light = higher value)
ldr.wiring: Photoresistor between 5 V and {pin}, 10 kΩ resistor between {pin} and GND.

ds18b20.title: DS18B20 probe
ds18b20.description: Temperature from −55 to 125 °C with ±0.5 °C, no calibration needed; the steel probe version can be immersed in water.
ds18b20.pinNote: With a 4.7 kΩ resistor between DATA and 5V.
ds18b20.wiring: Red to 5V, black to GND, yellow (DATA) to {pin}. A 4.7 kΩ resistor is needed between DATA and 5V (already present on boards with screw terminals).

gate.title: Photogate / digital input
gate.description: The instant an object blocks the beam, for periods, passage times and speeds; also works with a push button.
gate.pinNote: On D2 or D3 times are accurate to the µs; on other pins to the ms.
gate.blocked: When the beam is blocked, the output is
gate.width: Width of the object, for the speed
gate.wiring: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, OUT (or the module's D0) to {pin}.

hx711.title: Load cell + HX711
hx711.description: Mass and force from a load cell with an HX711 amplifier, up to 10 readings per second; it must be calibrated with a known weight.
hx711.autotareYes: yes: the initial load counts as 0
hx711.wiring: Cell: red E+, black E−, white A−, green A+ on the HX711. HX711: VCC 5V, GND, DT to {dt}, SCK to {sck}.

imu.title: MPU-6050 accelerometer
imu.description: Acceleration and angular velocity on 3 axes, up to 100 readings per second; shares the I2C bus with the display.
imu.sdaNote: Usually A4, shared with the display.
imu.gravity: Subtract gravity from the vertical axis
imu.wiring: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, SDA to {sda}, SCL to {scl}.

mlx.title: MLX90614 infrared thermometer
mlx.description: Temperature of a surface without touching it, from −70 to 380 °C, plus the sensor's own temperature; shares the I2C bus with the display.
mlx.sdaNote: Usually A4, shared with the display and the MPU-6050.
mlx.eps: Surface emissivity (skin 0.98, water 0.96, wood and plastic 0.90–0.95)
mlx.wiring: VIN (or VCC) to 5V, GND to GND, SDA to {sda}, SCL to {scl}. The sensor sees a cone of about 90°: hold it close to the surface, a few centimeters away.

oled.title: OLED display 64×32 (0.49")
oled.description: 0.49" I2C SSD1306 display (64×32 pixels): shows Arduino's status and, during a measurement, the time and the main value.
oled.wiring: VCC (or VDD) to 5V, GND to GND, SDA to {sda}, SCL to {scl}.

rgb.title: RGB LED
rgb.description: Blue: waiting for the app (blinking) or ready · blinking yellow: GPS or sensor searching · blinking red: problem · green: measurement running.
rgb.wiring: One 220 Ω resistor per color: R to {r}, G to {g}, B to {b}; long leg to {common}.

buzzer.title: Buzzer
buzzer.description: Every 3 s until something is ready: 1 beep waiting or stopped, 2 GPS or sensor searching, 3 problem. Silence: measurement running. With a Start/Stop button it stays quiet while waiting and gives a short, lower tick every 5 s while recording. Only a passive buzzer can change note: problems high, start/stop in the middle, the recording tick low.
buzzer.passive: passive (a different note for each signal)
buzzer.confirm: Confirmation beep at start and end
buzzer.wiring: + leg (the longer one, or “S”) to {pin}, − leg to GND.

button.title: Start/Stop button
button.measures: starts and stops the measurement from Arduino
button.description: A button on Arduino that works like “Start” and “Stop”: with the app connected (cable or Bluetooth) and with the SD card, where it starts and stops recording without a computer.
button.pinNote: The other leg goes to GND: the pull-up resistor is inside Arduino.
button.wiring: One leg of the button to {pin}, the other to GND.

sd.title: microSD card (records without a computer)
sd.description: Arduino records measurements on a microSD card, powered by a power bank or a battery: no cable, no phone. With the button you start and stop; without it, it records from when you switch it on. Then you import the files into the Notebook.
sd.wiring: microSD module (with regulator, runs on 5V): GND, VCC to 5V, MISO to D12, MOSI to D11, SCK to D13, CS to D10. Card formatted FAT32, up to 32 GB.

bt.rxdNote: With the 1 kΩ + 2 kΩ divider: the module's RXD takes 3.3 V.
bt.wiring: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, TXD to D0, RXD to D1 through the 1 kΩ + 2 kΩ divider.

hc06.title: Bluetooth HC-06 (classic)
hc06.description: Classic Bluetooth module: measure without a cable with Chrome on Android (not on iPhone). Arduino must be powered by a power bank.

ble.description: Bluetooth Low Energy module: measure without a cable with Chrome on computers and Android, and on iPhone with the Bluefy browser. Arduino must be powered by a power bank.

pmotion.title: Phone accelerometer and gyroscope
pmotion.description: The phone's motion sensors, up to about 60 readings per second. No Arduino: open the app on the phone.
pmotion.wiring: Open MosaicusNeo on the phone (Chrome on Android, Safari on iPhone) and press “Enable sensors”. On iPhone, confirm the permission.
pmotion.axes: Phone upright in front of you: x to the right, y up along the screen, z out of the screen. With the phone resting on the table a_z ≈ +9.8 m/s²: the accelerometer measures the table's reaction force, opposite to gravity.

psound.title: Microphone (frequency and level)
psound.description: Dominant frequency (50 Hz – 5 kHz) and relative level from the phone's or computer's microphone. The audio is not recorded.
psound.wiring: Uses the device's microphone: press “Enable sensors” and allow microphone access.

sps30.title: SPS30 particulate matter sensor
sps30.measures: fine dust PM1, PM2.5, PM4, PM10
sps30.description: Counts airborne particles with a laser and a small fan: mass concentration PM1.0, PM2.5, PM4 and PM10 in µg/m³, particle counts and typical particle size, one reading per second. Connects over I2C with its own cable.
sps30.sdaNote: Usually A4, shared with the other I2C devices.
sps30.wiring: With the JST ZHR-5 cable: pin 1 VDD to 5V, pin 2 SDA to {sda}, pin 3 SCL to {scl}, pin 4 SEL to GND (selects I2C), pin 5 GND to GND.

control.name: Controls
control.hint: to start and stop from Arduino

physics.ratePm: rate of change of the concentration

motion.title: Linear motion
motion.subtitle: Uniform and accelerated · HC-SR04
motion.tip: A cart on an inclined plane, with a flat target between 5 cm and 1 m from the sensor. Fitting a parabola to x(t) gives the acceleration.

harmonic.title: Harmonic motion
harmonic.subtitle: Oscillations · HC-SR04
harmonic.tip: A mass hanging from a spring, sensor on the floor pointing up, a piece of card under the mass. Fitting a damped sinusoid gives the period and the damping.

cooling.title: Cooling
cooling.subtitle: Newton's law · NTC thermistor
cooling.tip: Heat the thermistor in hot water or in a hot potato, then let it cool in air. Use the exponential fit with asymptote, or the straight line on ln(T − Tₐ).

humidity.title: Humidity & temperature
humidity.subtitle: Dew point · DHT11
humidity.tip: Breathe on the sensor: the humidity rises sharply and falls slowly. The exponential fit of the decay gives the time constant.

gpsmap.title: Temperature map
gpsmap.subtitle: GPS + DHT11 · phone via Bluetooth
gpsmap.wireless: Turn on the “Bluetooth” switch in the “Wiring” tab and choose the module (HC-06 or BLE): the diagram shows how to connect it. Power Arduino with a power bank; during the measurement the data is saved to the Notebook every 30 s.
gpsmap.fix: Outdoors the GPS finds the satellites in 30 s to a few minutes. Points without a position stay in the table but don't appear on the map.

phoneAcc.title: Accelerometer
phoneAcc.subtitle: Pendulum, elevator · phone
phoneAcc.tip: Pendulum: hang the phone from two strings, screen facing you, and let it swing; fitting a sinusoid to a_y gives the period. Elevator: phone on the floor, watch a_z when it starts and when it arrives.

phoneGyro.title: Gyroscope
phoneGyro.subtitle: Circular motion · phone
phoneGyro.tip: Phone on a swivel chair or a turntable: ω_z stays constant in uniform circular motion, and aₓ toward the center equals ω²r. In the pendulum the gyroscope oscillates with the pendulum's period, a_y at twice the frequency: why?

phoneSound.title: Frequency over time
phoneSound.subtitle: Doppler effect · microphone
phoneSound.tip: A car or a scooter sounding its horn as it passes you: the frequency drops as it goes by. From the frequency jump you get the speed: v ≈ c·Δf / (2f).

scope.title: Oscilloscope
scope.subtitle: Waveform of a sound
scope.wiring: The phone's or computer's microphone is all you need. The audio is neither recorded nor sent.

synth.subtitle: Makes a sound · keyboard, touch, tilt, HC-SR04
synth.wiring: HC-SR04 with TRIG to D12 and ECHO to D11, pointing up. Move your hand between 5 and 50 cm above the sensor.

escope.title: Electrical oscilloscope
escope.subtitle: Voltage on A0 · microphone, coil
escope.safe: Never mains power. The signal goes to A0.
escope.coil: Use single trigger and drop the magnet through the coil.

rig.phoneMix: Phone sensors can't be used together with Arduino components: keep them in a separate lab.
rig.onlyAccessories: There are only accessories (display, LED, button, SD card, Bluetooth): add at least one sensor.
rig.empty: The lab is empty: add at least one sensor.
rig.oneBluetooth: Only one Bluetooth module at a time: they all use D0 and D1. Remove the extra one.
rig.tooMany: Too many sensors: Arduino reads at most {max}. Remove some.
rig.maxType: {max, plural, =1 {You can use only one “{title}”: remove the extra one.} other {You can use at most # “{title}”: remove the extra ones.}}
rig.serialPin: {sensor}: D0 and D1 are reserved for the serial port (USB and Bluetooth). Choose another pin.
rig.fixedPin: {pin} is needed by {sensor} ({role}) and can't be changed: move {other} to another pin.
rig.pinTwice: {pin} is used twice ({other} and {sensor} · {role}). Change one of the two pins.
rig.minInterval: {sensor}: the minimum interval is {min} ms, that will be used.
rig.gpsDht: With the GPS, the DHT is read between one GPS message and the next: some readings may arrive late.
rig.sonars: Several ultrasonic sensors can pick up each other's echoes: point them in different directions.
rig.busFull: The I2C bus on {pin} ({role}) already has {max} devices: a breadboard column has only 5 connected holes (one for Arduino, {max} for the modules). Remove one I2C device.
rig.pinLocked: {sensor} needs {pin}, but it's taken by {other}, which can't move. Remove one of the two.
rig.noFreePin: No free {kind, select, analog {analog pin (A0–A5)} other {pin}} left for {sensor} ({role}).{i2c, select, yes { A4 and A5 carry the I2C bus.} other {}} Remove a component to free one.
rig.cantMove: {sensor} needs {pin}, which is used by {other}, and there's no free pin to move it to. Remove a component first.
rig.imuNoAddr: No free I2C address for another MPU-6050: 0x68 and 0x69 are already used ({list}).
rig.addrTaken: {sensor} needs I2C address 0x{addr}, which {other} already uses on the same bus, and it can’t be changed. Remove one of the two.
rig.addrClash: {a} and {b} have the same I2C address (0x{addr}) and would interfere. {imu, select, yes {Set the MPU-6050 to its other address in the advanced options.} other {Remove one of the two.}}
